permitsPage.title: Permit & Licensing Assistance
permitsPage.subtitle: Infrastructure Permits, Regulatory Coordination & Commercial Licensing Support
permitsPage.lead: We help project owners, ISPs, and contractors prepare permit documentation and coordinate with the relevant authorities and local stakeholders for infrastructure and commercial projects.
permitsPage.servicesDescription: Select the area that matches your project. Requirements differ by location, authority, and project type, so every engagement starts with a consultation.
permitsPage.card1: Assistance for road utilization permits, telecommunications infrastructure placement, and coordination with relevant road authorities.
permitsPage.card2: Support for aerial and underground fiber optic infrastructure, pole installation, and network deployment permissions.
permitsPage.card3: Assistance with excavation, duct installation, road crossing documentation, and restoration coordination.
permitsPage.card4: Coordination with village authorities, Banjar representatives, and local stakeholders for infrastructure projects.
permitsPage.card5: Assistance with land access agreements, infrastructure placement, lease coordination, and supporting documentation.
permitsPage.card6: Technical documentation and regulatory coordination for billboard and outdoor advertising installations.
permitsPage.card7: Assistance with route assessment, supporting documentation, and road-use dispensation for oversized or heavy cargo.
permitsPage.card8: Assistance and coordination for commercial content licensing and related usage permissions, including sports public viewing for venues.
permitsPage.noticeText: Jerco provides permit assistance and regulatory coordination. Permits and licenses are issued only by the competent authorities or, for commercial content, by the rights holders. Approval, requirements, fees, and processing times are determined by each issuer and may vary by location and project.
permitsPage.pvIntro: Showing live sports such as the Premier League, AFL, or NRL to guests in a bar, restaurant, hotel, villa, or beach club is a commercial public viewing. It generally requires a commercial license from the rights holder or its authorized distributor, separate from a home or personal subscription.
permitsPage.pvAvailability: Commercial rights, terms, and fees differ by competition, season, and territory, and are set by the rights holder.
permitsPage.pv1Text: List the competitions you want to show, venue type, capacity, and number of screens.
permitsPage.pv2Text: Find the rights holder or authorized distributor for commercial viewing of each competition in Indonesia.
permitsPage.pv3Text: Prepare venue data and supporting documents, and follow up the application with the licensor.
permitsPage.pv4Text: Set up receivers, IPTV, and TV distribution so licensed content reaches every screen in the venue.
permitsPage.pvDisclaimer: Jerco is not a broadcaster, rights holder, or official distributor, and is not affiliated with the leagues, organizers, or broadcasters mentioned. Competition names are trademarks of their respective owners.
permitsPage.processDescription: A structured workflow that keeps your documents, technical data, and coordination records organized from the first conversation onward.
permitsPage.step1Text: Discuss your project scope, location, and timeline to identify which permits may be relevant, based on the information you share.
permitsPage.step2Text: Help compile and organize supporting documents, drawings, route data, and technical attachments for the applicable process.
permitsPage.step3Text: Review technical data such as routes, KMZ/KML, drawings, and BOQ for completeness and consistency before submission.
permitsPage.step4Text: Support communication and coordination with the relevant authorities and local stakeholders throughout the process.
permitsPage.step5Text: Track progress, respond to requests for additional information, and keep records organized for your project files.
permitsPage.contactDescription: Share your project location, scope, and any existing drawings, route files (KMZ/KML), or documents. We will review them and discuss the next steps with you.
